solutionMethods.explanation:
Let \(\triangle ABC\) have its right angle at \(A\), and let \(M\) be the midpoint of hypotenuse \(BC\). The median-to-the-hypotenuse theorem gives
\[
AM=\frac{BC}{2}=BM=CM.
\]
Thus the circle centered at \(M\) with radius \(BC/2\) passes through all three vertices. It is the circumcircle, so its center is the midpoint of the hypotenuse, choice C.

reference.question: Where is the center of the circumcircle of a right triangle?
reference.solution:
Method 1: Identify the diameter

The chord subtending the right angle is a diameter, so the hypotenuse is the diameter of the circumcircle, and its center is the midpoint of the hypotenuse.

Method 2: Find a point equally far from the vertices

Let \(\triangle ABC\) have its right angle at \(A\), and let \(M\) be the midpoint of hypotenuse \(BC\). The median-to-the-hypotenuse theorem gives
\[
AM=\frac{BC}{2}=BM=CM.
\]
Thus the circle centered at \(M\) with radius \(BC/2\) passes through all three vertices. It is the circumcircle, so its center is the midpoint of the hypotenuse, choice C.
